title: Deal velocity failsafes and routing playbook
summary: Joint run-through of a co-sell routing playbook to accelerate a NimbleWave pilot. Covered hosted vs dedicated vs private, fallback policies, security gating (SOC2/KMS), and next steps: pricing, benchmarks, dataset handoff, and joint messaging. Action owners assigned and POC week proposed.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share joint pricing sheet and proposed committed capacity tiers by 2026-11-17
Devon Patel: Run 1-hour latency/cost benchmark using NimbleWave sample (1k token avg) and share logs by 2026-11-20
Laura Kim: Provide PHI-redacted sample dataset and acceptance criteria by 2026-11-19
Simon Hall: Draft co-sell one-pager and intro email template for reps by 2026-11-18
next_steps: Schedule POC kickoff for week of 2026-11-23 (Redwood + BlueBridge + NimbleWave)
Redwood to share security pack (SOC2 summary, KMS integrations, log/audit examples)
Partner to connect NimbleWave to two healthcare refs that used hybrid deployments
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-13 | 16:00 UTC | Duration 58m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (NimbleWave Head of Platform), Ethan Park (NWH Dir ML Eng), Priya Sethi (NWH VP Product), Simon Hall (BlueBridge Partner Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Joint alignment on co-sell routing and fallback playbook. Agreed POC scope and timelines. Security and data residency gating noted.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood, Devon on the call, and then from NimbleWave?
[00:12] Laura Kim: Laura here, hi.
[00:14] Ethan Park: Ethan, hi.
[00:16] Priya Sethi: Priya — good to meet you all.
[00:19] Simon Hall: Simon from BlueBridge, joining in.
[00:22] Devon Patel: Great. I'll kick us off with a quick framing of the routing playbook we suggested — the goal is to keep your latency SLAs under 200ms p50 for interactive features and still hit unit cost targets.
[00:36] Maya Chen: Right, and importantly the playbook gives three tiers: hosted fast-path, dedicated reserved, and private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated subsets. We want to route by policy: region, cost, and data residency.
[00:50] Ethan Park: Quick Q — for PHI flows, will that always force private? We have some mixed datasets, some de-identified, some not.
[00:57] Devon Patel: Good question. Short answer: it's policy-driven. If the data is PHI, we'd recommend Private (VPC) or Dedicated with encryption+KMS and strict audit logs. Hosted can be used for de-id workloads. There was a slight pause
[01:12] Priya Sethi: And what about fallback? Like if the dedicated pool is saturated, how do we keep the product online without leaking PHI to a hosted variant?
[01:22] Maya Chen: Exactly the core ask. Our playbook supports model-variant routing so you can fallback to an on-prem quantized variant or an in-region dedicated spare. The policy is configurable — you can opt to fail closed for PHI.
[01:35] Simon Hall: From partner perspective, BlueBridge usually suggests a grace capacity that we commit to for first 90 days so we avoid cold failovers. Redundancy, basically.
[01:45] Laura Kim: That sounds good. Could you — sorry Devon — could you speak to how caching and KV caching interacts with warm starts? We saw caching help a lot in your docs but worried about correctness w/ session data.
[02:00] Devon Patel: Sure. Redwood's prefix and KV cache is conservative for sensitive keys; it can be disabled per-route. The cache helps token cost, and during POC we'll show you how to whitelist/blacklist keys. Side note, transcription sometimes says K V cache as two letters.
[02:18] Ethan Park: Also, on model choice — you mentioned quantized variants. Do we get automatic quality regressions alerts? We can't sacrifice clinical accuracy.
[02:28] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to prompt sets. For POC we'll set up an eval harness to compare outputs between baseline and quantized runs, and set regression thresholds.
[02:41] Priya Sethi: Good. Timeline question — we want something live-ish by end of Q4. Is that realistic?
[02:47] Maya Chen: If we lock security and dataset handoff this week, POC kickoff week of Nov 23 is doable; then a 4-week POC can land a pilot by late Dec. That matches typical cadence.
[02:58] Simon Hall: Partner ask — can we have a co-branded one-pager for reps to push this into NimbleWave accounts? BlueBridge will hand-carry the motion.
[03:08] Maya Chen: Absolutely, Simon. Action: we'll draft messaging.
[03:11] [long pause / side chatter]
[03:30] Devon Patel: I want to run through an example routing flow: request comes in -> policy eval (is PHI? region? latency requirement?) -> route to host/dedicated/private. If dedicated is at capacity, fallback options are: scale-up, route to partner reserved pool, or fail closed — depending on policy.
[03:52] Ethan Park: How do we measure if routing decisions add overhead to latency? We can't add more than 10-15ms to decision path.
[03:59] Devon Patel: The policy eval is local and in-process; typically sub 5ms. The only heavy path is if we do model-variant translation or proxying. We'll share telemetry traces.
[04:16] Laura Kim: Can you share an example trace? A couple of our infra folks want to see X-Ray-ish data.
[04:22] Maya Chen: We'll include an example trace in the security pack — it has token-level timing and per-route breakdown.
[04:29] Priya Sethi: Pricing — high level, how does committed capacity work in a co-sell? We need number ranges to evaluate ROI.
[04:36] Maya Chen: We typically propose tiers: small (2-4 GPUs reserved), mid (6-12), enterprise (24+), with blended unit pricing and overage rates. For co-sell we can align discounts and partner uplift. I'll send a sample sheet.
[04:54] Simon Hall: BlueBridge likes to include a ramp schedule tied to revenue targets so it protects both sides.
[05:02] Devon Patel: For the POC, recommend a limited committed tranche plus burst capacity. It keeps cost predictable.
[05:09] Ethan Park: On compliance, SOC2 is table stakes. We also need proof of KMS/HSM integration and audit log retention.
[05:16] Maya Chen: Understood — security pack will include SOC2 summary, KMS options (AWS/GCP/Azure & HSM notes), and audit log samples.
[05:25] [background noise, someone shuffling papers]
[05:40] Laura Kim: One sticky point: our legal wants data residency — where logs live — and whether any tokenized traces go to third-party analytics.
[05:48] Maya Chen: Logs can be routed to your own SIEM in your VPC for Private deployments, and for Dedicated we support customer-managed log destinations. We do not surface raw prompts to analytics unless you opt-in.
[06:06] Priya Sethi: For model fallback, we worried about semantic drift from quantized models. How do we validate?
[06:13] Devon Patel: We'll run an eval set — your clinical prompts — and compute disagreement metrics and clinical-pass rates. If drift exceeds X% we'll halt fallback. We'll define X in the POC acceptance.
[06:31] Ethan Park: Do you have existing healthcare customers who went hybrid? Any case studies?
[06:36] Maya Chen: Yes, anonymized case study from a mid-size telehealth firm. We'll share a redacted win doc.
[06:44] Simon Hall: On governance, partners sometimes want a playbook for sales handoff — who owns objection handling on data residency?
[06:51] Maya Chen: Typically partner handles initial motion and AE owns security deep-dive with SE support. We'll codify that in the one-pager.
[07:05] [10 minute jump — discussion continues with specifics]
[17:22] Devon Patel: Ok jumping into POC scope: 1) latency/cost benchmark runs against 5 representative prompt types, 2) quality eval against 200 labeled prompts, 3) throughput stability test at 50 RPS for 30 minutes, 4) audit log validation.
[17:43] Laura Kim: For the labeled prompts we'll add edge cases — ambiguous clinical notes. We'll provide labels and a pass/fail rubric.
[17:52] Priya Sethi: On throughput, our peak is spiky — 80 RPS for short intervals. Can Redwood burst?
[17:59] Devon Patel: We support burst capacity; for Dedicated we can provision burst pools. For Private it depends on your infra sizing; BlueBridge can help sizing.
[18:10] Simon Hall: We'll include a burst sizing recommendation in the partner handoff doc.
[18:16] Ethan Park: About data handoff — what's the preferred format? JSONL? CSV?
[18:21] Devon Patel: JSONL with metadata fields is ideal. We accept S3 links or secure transfer to a VPC endpoint.
[18:29] Laura Kim: I'll aim to get a redacted S3 link by Thursday.
[18:33] Maya Chen: Great. Action logged.
[18:40] [crosstalk briefly as people agree on dates]
[19:05] Priya Sethi: A few technical clarifications — do you support model hot-swapping during a rollout? We want canary then full switchover.
[19:14] Devon Patel: Yes, canary and A/B supported. We also have automatic fallback on error rates and latency SLO breaches. There's a small transcription glitch: sometimes "canary" gets transcribed as "canarye".
[19:29] Ethan Park: For the eval harness, do you provide tools to run the tests or do we need to run locally?
[19:36] Maya Chen: Redwood provides an eval harness and JS/Python runners; we can host the harness or you can run it in your environment. We'll recommend hosting it in a secure workspace.
[19:49] Laura Kim: Security will push back on hosted, so we'll likely ask to run locally or in our VPC.
[19:55] Devon Patel: No problem — the harness can be run within your VPC and it will post only metrics back to Redwood if you prefer.
[20:05] [laughter]
[20:20] Simon Hall: From GTM — timeline for joint marketing? If POC starts Nov 23 and is successful, partner wants a joint webinar in Jan.
[20:30] Maya Chen: That's tight but doable. We can prep slides in Dec.
[20:35] Priya Sethi: Also need reference checks before we go broad — who can we talk to?
[20:40] Maya Chen: We'll include two references in the security pack; partner can add a third.
[20:46] Ethan Park: One more question — telemetry retention and retention deletion policy? We need 7-year retention for some audit trails?
[20:54] Devon Patel: That's long; our standard is 1 year, extended retention is an add-on. For enterprise agreements we can negotiate extended retention or ship logs to your archive.
[21:06] Laura Kim: We'll flag retention as a redline for legal.
[21:12] [brief pause]
[21:30] Maya Chen: Recap and next steps: we'll send pricing sheet, security pack, and a sample telemetry trace. Partner will draft the co-sell one-pager. NimbleWave to provide redacted data and acceptance criteria. POC kickoff week of Nov 23.
[21:50] Simon Hall: I'll get the one-pager draft out by Wednesday.
[21:54] Laura Kim: I'll push the data request internally and try for Thursday.
[21:59] Priya Sethi: Legal will look for retention and residency clauses; we'll come back with a list.
[22:05] Devon Patel: I'll start setting up the benchmark harness and will need a small credentialed S3 link.
[22:12] Maya Chen: Great — anything else?
[22:16] Ethan Park: Quick note — we may want a private demo of model outputs with clinical redaction off-line. I'll follow up.
[22:23] Maya Chen: We can do that in the POC environment.
[22:27] [closing pleasantries]
[22:40] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and items.
[22:45] Laura Kim: Thanks all.
[22:47] Simon Hall: Thanks, bye.
[22:50] [meeting end — recording stops]

Notes on transcription: there are occasional mis-hearings ("K V cache", "canarye"). Speaker labels largely accurate though sometimes overlapping speech was collapsed. The transcript above is a faithful export with natural filler and interruptions.
